## 1. What does this tool do? *grex* is a library as well as a command-line utility that is meant to simplify the often complicated and tedious task of creating regular expressions. It does so by automatically generating a single regular expression from user-provided test cases. The resulting expression is guaranteed to match the test cases which it was generated from. This project has started as a Rust port of the JavaScript tool [*regexgen*](https://github.com/devongovett/regexgen) written by [Devon Govett](https://github.com/devongovett). Although a lot of further useful features could be added to it, its development was apparently ceased several years ago. The plan is now to add these new features to *grex* as Rust really shines when it comes to command-line tools. *grex* offers all features that *regexgen* provides, and more. The philosophy of this project is to generate the most specific regular expression possible by default which exactly matches the given input only and nothing else. With the use of command-line flags (in the CLI tool) or preprocessing methods (in the library), more generalized expressions can be created. The produced expressions are [Perl-compatible regular expressions](https://www.pcre.org) which are also compatible with the regular expression parser in Rust's [*regex* crate](https://crates.io/crates/regex). Other regular expression parsers or respective libraries from other programming languages have not been tested so far, but they ought to be mostly compatible as well. ## 2. Do I still need to learn to write regexes then? **Definitely, yes!** Using the standard settings, *grex* produces a regular expression that is guaranteed to match only the test cases given as input and nothing else. This has been verified by [property tests](https://github.com/pemistahl/grex/blob/main/tests/property_tests.rs). However, if the conversion to shorthand character classes such as `\w` is enabled, the resulting regex matches a much wider scope of test cases. Detailed explanations of the available settings are provided in the [library section](#52-the-library).
All settings can be freely combined with each other.

### 5.1 The command-line tool

Test cases are passed either directly (`grex a b c`) or from a file (`grex -f test_cases.txt`).
*grex* is able to receive its input from Unix pipelines as well, e.g. `cat test_cases.txt | grex -`.

Note:

U+0079 (Latin Small Letter Y)
U+0306 (Combining Breve)

Input containing blank space must be

### 5.2 The library

#### 5.2.1 Default settings

Test cases are passed either from a collection via [`RegExpBuilder::from()`](https://docs.rs/grex/1.4.6/grex/struct.RegExpBuilder.html#method.from) 
or from a file via [`RegExpBuilder::from_file()`](https://docs.rs/grex/1.4.6/grex/struct.RegExpBuilder.html#method.from_file).
If read from a file, each test case must be on a separate line. Lines may be ended with either a newline `\n` or a carriage
return with a line feed `\r\n`.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "aa", "aaa"]).build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^a(?:aa?)?$");
```

#### 5.2.2 Convert to character classes

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "aa", "123"])
    .with_conversion_of_digits()
    .with_conversion_of_words()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^(\\d\\d\\d|\\w(?:\\w)?)$");
```

#### 5.2.3 Convert repeated substrings

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["aa", "bcbc", "defdefdef"])
    .with_conversion_of_repetitions()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^(?:a{2}|(?:bc){2}|(?:def){3})$");
```

By default, *grex* converts each substring this way which is at least a single character long 
and which is subsequently repeated at least once. You can customize these two parameters if you like.

In the following example, the test case `aa` is not converted to `a{2}` because the repeated substring 
`a` has a length of 1, but the minimum substring length has been set to 2.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["aa", "bcbc", "defdefdef"])
    .with_conversion_of_repetitions()
    .with_minimum_substring_length(2)
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^(?:aa|(?:bc){2}|(?:def){3})$");
```

Setting a minimum number of 2 repetitions in the next example, only the test case `defdefdef` will be
converted because it is the only one that is repeated twice.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["aa", "bcbc", "defdefdef"])
    .with_conversion_of_repetitions()
    .with_minimum_repetitions(2)
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^(?:bcbc|aa|(?:def){3})$");
```

#### 5.2.4 Escape non-ascii characters

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["You smell like 💩."])
    .with_escaping_of_non_ascii_chars(false)
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^You smell like \\u{1f4a9}\\.$");
```

Old versions of JavaScript do not support unicode escape sequences for the astral code planes 
(range `U+010000` to `U+10FFFF`). In order to support these symbols in JavaScript regular 
expressions, the conversion to surrogate pairs is necessary. More information on that matter 
can be found [here](https://mathiasbynens.be/notes/javascript-unicode).

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["You smell like 💩."])
    .with_escaped_non_ascii_chars(true)
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "^You smell like \\u{d83d}\\u{dca9}\\.$");
```

#### 5.2.5 Case-insensitive matching

The regular expressions that *grex* generates are case-sensitive by default.
Case-insensitive matching can be enabled like so:

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["big", "BIGGER"])
    .with_case_insensitive_matching()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "(?i)^big(?:ger)?$");
```

#### 5.2.6 Capturing Groups

Non-capturing groups are used by default. 
Extending the previous example, you can switch to capturing groups instead.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["big", "BIGGER"])
    .with_case_insensitive_matching()
    .with_capturing_groups()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "(?i)^big(ger)?$");
```

#### 5.2.7 Verbose mode

If you find the generated regular expression hard to read, you can enable verbose mode.
The expression is then put on multiple lines and indented to make it more pleasant to the eyes.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;
use indoc::indoc;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "b", "bcd"])
    .with_verbose_mode()
    .build();

assert_eq!(regexp, indoc!(
    r#"
    (?x)
    ^
      (?:
        b
        (?:
          cd
        )?
        |
        a
      )
    $"#
));
```

#### 5.2.8 Disable anchors

By default, the anchors `^` and `$` are put around every generated regular expression in order
to ensure that it matches only the test cases given as input. Often enough, however, it is
desired to use the generated pattern as part of a larger one. For this purpose, the anchors
can be disabled, either separately or both of them.

```rust
use grex::RegExpBuilder;

let regexp = RegExpBuilder::from(&["a", "aa", "aaa"])
    .without_anchors()
    .build();
assert_eq!(regexp, "a(?:aa?)?");
```

# ------------------------- low-level character handling ----------------------

def is_word_char(ch: str) -> bool:
    if ch in ('\u200c', '\u200d'):
        return True
    cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
    return ch.isalpha() or ch.isdecimal() or cat.startswith('M') or cat == 'Pc'

def lower_simple(s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        lo = ch.lower()
        if len(lo) == 1:
            out.append(lo)
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)

def unicode_escape(cp: int) -> str:
    return "\\u{" + format(cp, 'x') + "}"

def outside_escape(ch: str, escape_non_ascii: bool, surrogates: bool, verbose: bool=False):
    cp = ord(ch)
    if escape_non_ascii and cp > 0x7f:
        if surrogates and cp > 0xffff:
            u = cp - 0x10000
            hi = 0xd800 + (u >> 10)
            lo = 0xdc00 + (u & 0x3ff)
            # The original treats the surrogate-pair spelling as one atom, but
            # it must be grouped when quantified.
            return unicode_escape(hi) + unicode_escape(lo), False, False
        return unicode_escape(cp), False, True
    if ch == '\n': return "\\n", True, True
    if ch == '\r': return "\\r", True, True
    if ch == '\t': return "\\t", True, True
    if ch == '\v': return "\\v", True, True
    if ch == '\f': return "\\f", True, True
    if verbose and ch == ' ':
        return "\\ ", True, True
    if verbose and ch == '#':
        return "\\#", True, True
    if ch in r".\+*?()|[]{}^$-":
        return "\\" + ch, True, True
    return ch, True, True

    if ch == '\n': return "\\n"
    if ch == '\r': return "\\r"
    if ch == '\t': return "\\t"
    if ch == '\v': return "\\v"
    if ch == '\f': return "\\f"
    if ch in ('\\', '[', ']', '^', '-'):
        return "\\" + ch
    return ch

def build_char_class(chars: list[str]) -> str:
    vals = sorted(set(chars), key=lambda c: ord(c))
    parts = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(vals):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(vals) and ord(vals[j+1]) == ord(vals[j]) + 1:
            j += 1
        run_len = j - i + 1
        if run_len >= 3:
            parts.append(class_char_escape(vals[i], True) + '-' + class_char_escape(vals[j], True))
        else:
            for k in range(i, j+1):
                parts.append(class_char_escape(vals[k], False))
        i = j + 1
    return '[' + ''.join(parts) + ']'

class Expr:
    def render(self, opt: Options, verbose_token: bool=False) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError
    def max_len(self) -> int: return 0
    def min_len(self) -> int: return 0
    def min_string(self) -> str: return ''
    def contains_repeat(self) -> bool: return False
    def simple_inline(self) -> bool: return False

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Empty(Expr):
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False): return ''
    def simple_inline(self): return True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Atom(Expr):
    key: Any
    display: str
    verbose_display: str
    raw: str = ''
    charclassable: bool = False
    direct_quant: bool = True
    shorthand: bool = False
    orig_len: int = 1
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        return self.verbose_display if verbose_token else self.display
    def max_len(self): return self.orig_len
    def min_len(self): return self.orig_len
    def min_string(self): return self.raw if self.raw else self.display
    def simple_inline(self): return True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CharClass(Expr):
    chars: tuple
    text: str
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False): return self.text
    def max_len(self): return 1
    def min_len(self): return 1
    def min_string(self): return min(self.chars, key=lambda c: ord(c)) if self.chars else ''
    def simple_inline(self): return True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Concat(Expr):
    parts: tuple
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        return ''.join(p.render(opt, verbose_token) for p in self.parts if not isinstance(p, Empty))
    def max_len(self): return sum(p.max_len() for p in self.parts)
    def min_len(self): return sum(p.min_len() for p in self.parts)
    def min_string(self): return ''.join(p.min_string() for p in self.parts)
    def contains_repeat(self): return any(p.contains_repeat() for p in self.parts)
    def simple_inline(self): return all(p.simple_inline() for p in self.parts)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Alt(Expr):
    alts: tuple
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        gp = '(' if opt.capture_groups else '(?:'
        return gp + '|'.join(a.render(opt, verbose_token) for a in self.alts) + ')'
    def max_len(self): return max((a.max_len() for a in self.alts), default=0)
    def min_len(self): return min((a.min_len() for a in self.alts), default=0)
    def min_string(self): return min((a.min_string() for a in self.alts), default='')
    def contains_repeat(self): return any(a.contains_repeat() for a in self.alts)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptionalExpr(Expr):
    child: Expr
    style: str = 'normal'  # 'normal' or 'prefix'

        s = self.child.render(opt, verbose_token)
        gp = '(' if opt.capture_groups else '(?:'
        if self.style == 'prefix':

            # aggressively by grex.
            if isinstance(self.child, Atom) and len(self.child.raw) == 1 and self.child.direct_quant and not self.child.shorthand:

            return gp + s + ')?'
        if isinstance(self.child, (Atom, CharClass)) and getattr(self.child, 'direct_quant', True):
            return s + '?'
        if isinstance(self.child, Alt):
            return s + '?'
        return gp + s + ')?'
    def max_len(self): return self.child.max_len()
    def min_len(self): return 0
    def min_string(self): return ''
    def contains_repeat(self): return self.child.contains_repeat()
    def simple_inline(self):
        return isinstance(self.child, (Atom, CharClass)) or (isinstance(self.child, Concat) and self.child.simple_inline() and self.style=='normal')

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RepeatExpr(Expr):
    base: Expr
    min_count: int
    max_count: int
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        bs = self.base.render(opt, verbose_token)
        if self.min_count == self.max_count:
            q = '{%d}' % self.min_count
        else:
            q = '{%d,%d}' % (self.min_count, self.max_count)
        direct = isinstance(self.base, (Atom, CharClass)) and getattr(self.base, 'direct_quant', True)
        if direct:
            return bs + q
        gp = '(' if opt.capture_groups else '(?:'
        return gp + bs + ')' + q
    def max_len(self): return self.base.max_len() * self.max_count
    def min_len(self): return self.base.min_len() * self.min_count
    def min_string(self): return self.base.min_string() * self.min_count
    def contains_repeat(self): return True
    def simple_inline(self):
        return isinstance(self.base, (Atom, CharClass)) and getattr(self.base, 'direct_quant', True)

# Sequence item is an atom or a repetition atom. Both are hashable.
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RepeatItem:
    base_items: tuple
    base_expr: Expr
    count: int
    orig_len: int
    def to_expr(self):
        return RepeatExpr(self.base_expr, self.count, self.count)
    def max_len(self): return self.orig_len * self.count
    def min_len(self): return self.orig_len * self.count
    def min_string(self): return self.base_expr.min_string() * self.count

# -------------------------- preprocessing -----------------------------------

def shorthand_atom(name: str) -> Atom:
    return Atom(('sh', name), '\\' + name, '\\' + name, raw='\\'+name, charclassable=False, direct_quant=True, shorthand=True)

def make_literal_atom(ch: str, opt: Options) -> Atom:
    disp, cc, direct = outside_escape(ch, opt.escape, opt.surrogates, False)
    vdisp, _, _ = outside_escape(ch, opt.escape, opt.surrogates, True)
    # Non-ASCII escaped atoms are not put into character classes.
    charclassable = cc and not (opt.escape and ord(ch) > 0x7f)
    return Atom(('lit', ch, opt.escape, opt.surrogates), disp, vdisp, raw=ch, charclassable=charclassable, direct_quant=direct, shorthand=False)

def convert_char(ch: str, opt: Options):
    # documented precedence
    isdig = ch.isdecimal()
    issp = ch.isspace()
    isword = is_word_char(ch)
    if opt.digits and isdig:
        return shorthand_atom('d')
    if opt.spaces and issp:
        return shorthand_atom('s')
    if opt.words and isword:
        return shorthand_atom('w')
    if opt.non_digits and not isdig:
        return shorthand_atom('D')
    if opt.non_words and not isword:
        return shorthand_atom('W')
    if opt.non_spaces and not issp:
        return shorthand_atom('S')
    return make_literal_atom(ch, opt)

def preprocess_string(s: str, opt: Options):
    if opt.ignore_case:
        s = lower_simple(s)
    return tuple(convert_char(ch, opt) for ch in s)

# -------------------------- repetition detection ----------------------------

def item_key(x):
    if isinstance(x, Atom): return ('A', x.key)
    if isinstance(x, RepeatItem): return ('R', tuple(item_key(i) for i in x.base_items), x.count)
    return ('?', repr(x))

def items_equal_slice(seq, i, j, L):
    for k in range(L):
        if item_key(seq[i+k]) != item_key(seq[j+k]):
            return False
    return True

def expr_from_sequence_items(items: tuple, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    # Render a repeated unit using the ordinary generator, but without trying
    # suffix alternatives. This gives compact nested repetitions such as
    # (?:a{5}b){2} and (?:\d\s\w{3}\s){2}.
    if not items:
        return Empty()
    parts = []
    for it in items:
        if isinstance(it, Atom): parts.append(it)
        else: parts.append(it.to_expr())
    return concat_expr(parts)

def compress_repetitions(seq: tuple, opt: Options) -> tuple:
    n = len(seq)
    if n == 0: return seq
    candidates = []
    minL = max(1, opt.min_substring_length)
    threshold = opt.min_repetitions + 1
    for i in range(n):
        maxL = (n - i) // threshold

        selected.append((i, L, c, span))

            unit_orig = tuple(seq[i:i+L])
            unit_compressed = compress_repetitions(unit_orig, opt)
            base_expr = expr_from_sequence_items(unit_compressed, opt)
            out.append(RepeatItem(unit_orig, base_expr, c, L))
            i += span
        else:
            out.append(seq[i])
            i += 1
    return tuple(out)

# ----------------------------- generation -----------------------------------

def concat_expr(parts: list[Expr]) -> Expr:
    flat = []
    for p in parts:
        if isinstance(p, Empty):
            continue
        if isinstance(p, Concat):
            flat.extend(p.parts)
        else:
            flat.append(p)
    if not flat: return Empty()
    if len(flat) == 1: return flat[0]
    return Concat(tuple(flat))

def alt_expr(alts: list[Expr], opt: Options, sort=True) -> Expr:
    # de-duplicate by compact rendering
    seen = set(); uniq = []
    for a in alts:
        k = a.render(opt, False)
        if k not in seen:
            seen.add(k); uniq.append(a)
    if sort:
        uniq.sort(key=lambda e: sort_key(e, opt))
    if not uniq: return Empty()
    if len(uniq) == 1: return uniq[0]
    return Alt(tuple(uniq))

def sort_key(e: Expr, opt: Options):
    # Default grex output generally lists longer branches first; when
    # repetition conversion is enabled, plain alternatives tend to precede
    # quantified ones and quantified alternatives are ordered by matched size.
    if opt.repetitions:
        rep = 1 if e.contains_repeat() else 0
        if rep:
            return (1, e.min_len(), e.min_string(), e.render(opt, False))
        return (0, -e.max_len(), e.min_len(), e.min_string(), e.render(opt, False))
    return (-e.max_len(), e.min_len(), e.min_string(), e.render(opt, False))

def atom_expr_from_item(it):
    if isinstance(it, Atom): return it
    if isinstance(it, RepeatItem): return it.to_expr()
    raise TypeError

def base_expr_for_items(items: tuple, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    return expr_from_sequence_items(items, opt)

def ranges_from_counts(counts: list[int]):
    counts = sorted(set(counts))
    ranges = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(counts):
        j = i
        while j+1 < len(counts) and counts[j+1] == counts[j]+1:
            j += 1
        ranges.append((counts[i], counts[j]))
        i = j+1
    return ranges

def atom_alternation(items: list, opt: Options, allow_mixed_class=True) -> Expr:
    # This handles a set of one-position alternatives, including character
    # classes and repeat-count ranges.
    # First, group RepeatItems with identical bases.
    used = [False]*len(items)
    exprs = []
    # Repeat groups
    repeat_groups: Dict[Any, list] = {}
    repeat_base: Dict[Any, tuple] = {}
    for idx,it in enumerate(items):
        if isinstance(it, RepeatItem):
            k = tuple(item_key(x) for x in it.base_items)
            repeat_groups.setdefault(k, []).append(it.count)
            repeat_base[k] = it.base_items
            used[idx]=True
    # Include a count of one for single-token literal bases only; this mirrors
    # the compact a{1,n} output while keeping ab|(?:ab){2,n} separate.
    for k, counts in list(repeat_groups.items()):
        base_items = repeat_base[k]
        if len(base_items)==1:
            for idx,it in enumerate(items):
                if not used[idx] and item_key(it)==item_key(base_items[0]):
                    counts.append(1); used[idx]=True
    for k, counts in repeat_groups.items():
        base = base_expr_for_items(repeat_base[k], opt)
        for a,b in ranges_from_counts(counts):
            if a==b==1:
                exprs.append(base)
            else:
                exprs.append(RepeatExpr(base,a,b))
    remaining = [it for idx,it in enumerate(items) if not used[idx]]
    # Char class grouping for literal atoms.
    literal_atoms = [it for it in remaining if isinstance(it, Atom) and it.charclassable]
    non_literals = [it for it in remaining if not (isinstance(it, Atom) and it.charclassable)]
    if literal_atoms:
        group_as_class = False
        if len(literal_atoms) >= 2 and not non_literals:
            group_as_class = True
        elif len(literal_atoms) >= 2 and allow_mixed_class:
            # Escaped unicode alternatives are mixed with classes; shorthand
            # conversions usually keep alphanumeric literals separate.  For
            # punctuation, a class is still what grex prints.
            has_shorthand = any(isinstance(x, Atom) and x.shorthand for x in non_literals)
            if not has_shorthand:
                group_as_class = True
            else:
                if all((not a.raw.isalnum()) for a in literal_atoms):
                    group_as_class = True
        if group_as_class:
            chars = tuple(a.raw for a in literal_atoms)
            exprs.append(CharClass(chars, build_char_class(list(chars))))
        else:
            exprs.extend(literal_atoms)
    exprs.extend(atom_expr_from_item(x) for x in non_literals)
    return alt_expr(exprs, opt, sort=True)

def seq_to_expr(seq: tuple, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    return concat_expr([atom_expr_from_item(x) for x in seq])

def language_key(seqs: Set[tuple]):
    return tuple(sorted(tuple(item_key(x) for x in s) for s in seqs))

def generate_prefix_normal(seqs_in, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    seqs = set(seqs_in)
    if not seqs:
        return Empty()
    if len(seqs)==1:
        return seq_to_expr(next(iter(seqs)), opt)
    has_empty = tuple() in seqs
    nonempty = {s for s in seqs if s}
    if not nonempty:
        return Empty()

    # If every sequence is a single item, render this level directly.
    if all(len(s)==1 for s in nonempty) and not has_empty:
        return atom_alternation([s[0] for s in nonempty], opt)

    # Build first-token groups, merging transitions with identical tail languages.
    tail_to_tokens: Dict[Any, list] = {}
    tailsets: Dict[Any, Set[tuple]] = {}
    for s in nonempty:
        first, tail = s[0], s[1:]
        k = language_key({tail})
        # Actually merge by the full set of tails for a token below; first collect
        # by first token then invert.
    token_to_tails: Dict[Any, Set[tuple]] = {}
    token_obj: Dict[Any, Any] = {}
    for s in nonempty:
        first, tail = s[0], s[1:]
        k = item_key(first)
        token_to_tails.setdefault(k,set()).add(tail)
        token_obj[k]=first
    inv: Dict[Any, list] = {}
    inv_tails: Dict[Any, Set[tuple]] = {}
    for k,tails in token_to_tails.items():
        lk = language_key(tails)
        inv.setdefault(lk,[]).append(token_obj[k])
        inv_tails[lk]=tails
    terms = []
    for lk,tokens in inv.items():
        token_expr = atom_alternation(tokens, opt)
        tail_expr = generate_language(inv_tails[lk], opt)
        terms.append(concat_expr([token_expr, tail_expr]))
    body = alt_expr(terms, opt, sort=True)
    if has_empty:
        return OptionalExpr(body, 'normal')
    return body

def generate_prefix_before_suffix(seqs_in, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    seqs = set(seqs_in)
    if tuple() not in seqs:
        return generate_prefix_normal(seqs, opt)
    nonempty = {s for s in seqs if s}
    if not nonempty:
        return Empty()
    # Build nonempty alternatives in normal fashion, but keep top branches.
    expr = generate_prefix_normal(nonempty, opt)
    if isinstance(expr, Alt):
        branches = list(expr.alts)
    else:
        branches = [expr]
    branches.sort(key=lambda e: sort_key(e, opt))
    if len(branches)==1:
        return OptionalExpr(branches[0], 'prefix')
    # Select a branch to remain mandatory: maximum length, ties last in order.
    maxlen = max(b.max_len() for b in branches)
    cand_indices = [i for i,b in enumerate(branches) if b.max_len()==maxlen]
    sel = cand_indices[-1]
    selected = branches[sel]
    others = [b for i,b in enumerate(branches) if i!=sel]
    opt_group = OptionalExpr(alt_expr(others, opt, sort=True), 'prefix')
    if sel == 0:
        ordered = [selected, opt_group]
    else:
        ordered = [opt_group, selected]
    return alt_expr(ordered, opt, sort=False)

def common_suffix(seqs: Set[tuple]) -> tuple:
    if not seqs or any(len(s)==0 for s in seqs): return tuple()
    minlen = min(len(s) for s in seqs)
    out = []
    for i in range(1, minlen+1):
        vals = {item_key(s[-i]) for s in seqs}
        if len(vals)==1:
            out.append(next(iter(seqs))[-i])
        else:
            break
    return tuple(reversed(out))

def has_literal_then_class(e: Expr) -> bool:
    # Quirk: grex generally does not choose a common-suffix optionalization when
    # the optional prefix is a single concatenation like a[bc] or ab[cd].
    if isinstance(e, OptionalExpr):
        child = e.child
    else:
        child = e
    if isinstance(child, Concat):
        seen_first_lit = False
        for idx,p in enumerate(child.parts):
            if idx==0 and isinstance(p, Atom) and not p.shorthand and p.charclassable:
                seen_first_lit = True
            elif seen_first_lit and isinstance(p, CharClass):
                return True
    return False

def generate_language(seqs_in, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    seqs = set(seqs_in)
    if not seqs: return Empty()
    prefix = generate_prefix_normal(seqs, opt)
    suff = common_suffix(seqs)
    if suff:
        prefixes = {s[:-len(suff)] for s in seqs}
        pre_expr = generate_prefix_before_suffix(prefixes, opt)
        suffix_expr = seq_to_expr(suff, opt)
        cand = concat_expr([pre_expr, suffix_expr])
        # Avoid the known a[bc] optionalization quirk.
        disallow = isinstance(pre_expr, OptionalExpr) and has_literal_then_class(pre_expr)
        if not disallow:
            if len(cand.render(opt, False)) <= len(prefix.render(opt, False)):
                return cand
    return prefix

# ------------------------- verbose rendering --------------------------------

def group_open(opt: Options): return '(' if opt.capture_groups else '(?:'

def quant_suffix_for_repeat(e: RepeatExpr):
    if e.min_count == e.max_count: return '{%d}' % e.min_count
    return '{%d,%d}' % (e.min_count, e.max_count)

def verbose_lines_expr(e: Expr, opt: Options, indent: int) -> list[str]:
    sp = ' ' * indent
    if e.simple_inline():
        return [sp + e.render(opt, True)]
    if isinstance(e, Alt):
        lines = [sp + group_open(opt)]
        for idx,a in enumerate(e.alts):
            if idx:
                lines.append(' '*(indent+2) + '|')
            lines.extend(verbose_lines_expr(a, opt, indent+2))
        lines.append(sp + ')')
        return lines
    if isinstance(e, Concat):
        lines=[]; buf=''
        def flush():
            nonlocal buf
            if buf:
                lines.append(sp + buf); buf=''
        for p in e.parts:
            if p.simple_inline():
                buf += p.render(opt, True)
            else:
                flush(); lines.extend(verbose_lines_expr(p,opt,indent))
        flush()
        return lines if lines else [sp]
    if isinstance(e, OptionalExpr):
        # Complex optional group.
        child = e.child
        if isinstance(child, Alt):
            inner = verbose_lines_expr(child, opt, indent)
            # append ? to the closing line of that group
            inner[-1] += '?'
            return inner
        lines = [sp + group_open(opt)]
        lines.extend(verbose_lines_expr(child, opt, indent+2))
        lines.append(sp + ')?')
        return lines
    if isinstance(e, RepeatExpr):
        if e.simple_inline():
            return [sp + e.render(opt, True)]
        q = quant_suffix_for_repeat(e)
        lines = [sp + group_open(opt)]
        lines.extend(verbose_lines_expr(e.base, opt, indent+2))
        lines.append(sp + ')' + q)
        return lines
    return [sp + e.render(opt, True)]

def render_verbose(body: Expr, opt: Options, start_anchor: bool, end_anchor: bool) -> str:
    flag = '(?ix)' if opt.ignore_case else '(?x)'
    lines=[flag]
    if start_anchor: lines.append('^')
    lines.extend(verbose_lines_expr(body, opt, 2))
    if end_anchor: lines.append('$')
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

# ------------------------- colorizer -----------------------------------------

def colorize_regex(s: str) -> str:
    RESET='\x1b[0m'; ANCH='\x1b[1;33m'; GROUP='\x1b[1;32m'; ALT='\x1b[1;31m'
    Q='\x1b[1;35m'; QBR='\x1b[104;37m'; CLS='\x1b[1;36m'; SH='\x1b[103;30m'; FLAG='\x1b[40;93m'
    out=[]; i=0; n=len(s)
    while i<n:
        if s.startswith('(?ix)', i) or s.startswith('(?i)', i) or s.startswith('(?x)', i):
            if s.startswith('(?ix)', i): tok='(?ix)'
            elif s.startswith('(?i)', i): tok='(?i)'
            else: tok='(?x)'
            out.append(FLAG+tok+RESET); i+=len(tok); continue
        ch=s[i]
        if ch=='\\':
            if i+1<n and s[i+1] in 'dDsSwW':
                out.append(SH+s[i:i+2]+RESET); i+=2; continue
            # leave other escapes plain, including \u{...}
            if i+1<n:
                out.append(s[i:i+2]); i+=2; continue
        if ch in '^$': out.append(ANCH+ch+RESET); i+=1; continue
        if s.startswith('(?:', i): out.append(GROUP+'(?:'+RESET); i+=3; continue
        if ch in '()': out.append(GROUP+ch+RESET); i+=1; continue
        if ch=='|': out.append(ALT+ch+RESET); i+=1; continue
        if ch in '?*+': out.append(Q+ch+RESET); i+=1; continue
        if ch=='{':
            j=s.find('}', i+1)
            if j!=-1:
                out.append(QBR+s[i:j+1]+RESET); i=j+1; continue
        if ch=='[':
            out.append(CLS+'['+RESET); i+=1; continue
        if ch==']':
            out.append(CLS+']'+RESET); i+=1; continue
        out.append(ch); i+=1
    return ''.join(out)

# ----------------------------- CLI -------------------------------------------

def eprint(msg):
    sys.stderr.write(msg)

def parse_uint(val: str, optname: str, label: str):
    try:
        if val.startswith('-'):
            raise ValueError
        n=int(val)
    except Exception:
        eprint(f"error: invalid value '{val}' for '--{optname} <{label}>': Value is not a valid unsigned integer\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    if n==0:
        eprint(f"error: invalid value '0' for '--{optname} <{label}>': Value must not be zero\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    return n

def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> Options:
    opt=Options(inputs=[])
    known_short=set('dDsSwWerxci ghvf'.replace(' ',''))
    i=0
    while i < len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a == '-h': print(SHORT_HELP, end=''); sys.exit(0)
        if a == '--help': print(LONG_HELP, end=''); sys.exit(0)
        if a == '-v' or a == '--version': print(VERSION); sys.exit(0)
        if a.startswith('--min-repetitions='):
            opt.min_repetitions=parse_uint(a.split('=',1)[1], 'min-repetitions', 'QUANTITY'); i+=1; continue
        if a == '--min-repetitions':
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint("error: a value is required for '--min-repetitions <QUANTITY>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"); sys.exit(2)
            opt.min_repetitions=parse_uint(argv[i+1], 'min-repetitions', 'QUANTITY'); i+=2; continue
        if a.startswith('--min-substring-length='):
            opt.min_substring_length=parse_uint(a.split('=',1)[1], 'min-substring-length', 'LENGTH'); i+=1; continue
        if a == '--min-substring-length':
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint("error: a value is required for '--min-substring-length <LENGTH>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"); sys.exit(2)
            opt.min_substring_length=parse_uint(argv[i+1], 'min-substring-length', 'LENGTH'); i+=2; continue
        if a.startswith('--file='):
            opt.file=a.split('=',1)[1]; i+=1; continue
        if a in ('-f','--file'):
            if i+1>=len(argv):
                eprint("error: a value is required for '--file <FILE>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"); sys.exit(2)
            opt.file=argv[i+1]; i+=2; continue
        longmap={'--digits':'digits','--non-digits':'non_digits','--spaces':'spaces','--non-spaces':'non_spaces','--words':'words','--non-words':'non_words','--escape':'escape','--with-surrogates':'surrogates','--repetitions':'repetitions','--no-start-anchor':'no_start_anchor','--no-end-anchor':'no_end_anchor','--verbose':'verbose','--colorize':'colorize','--ignore-case':'ignore_case','--capture-groups':'capture_groups'}
        if a == '--no-anchors':
            opt.no_start_anchor=True; opt.no_end_anchor=True; i+=1; continue
        if a in longmap:
            setattr(opt, longmap[a], True); i+=1; continue
        # short flag clusters: only if every character is a known short flag
        if a.startswith('-') and len(a)>2 and all(ch in known_short for ch in a[1:]):
            chars=list(a[1:]); consumed_file=False
            for ch in chars:
                if ch=='h': print(SHORT_HELP,end=''); sys.exit(0)
                if ch=='v': print(VERSION); sys.exit(0)
                if ch=='f':
                    if i+1>=len(argv):
                        eprint("error: a value is required for '--file <FILE>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"); sys.exit(2)
                    opt.file=argv[i+1]; consumed_file=True
                elif ch=='d': opt.digits=True
                elif ch=='D': opt.non_digits=True
                elif ch=='s': opt.spaces=True
                elif ch=='S': opt.non_spaces=True
                elif ch=='w': opt.words=True
                elif ch=='W': opt.non_words=True
                elif ch=='e': opt.escape=True
                elif ch=='r': opt.repetitions=True
                elif ch=='x': opt.verbose=True
                elif ch=='c': opt.colorize=True
                elif ch=='i': opt.ignore_case=True
                elif ch=='g': opt.capture_groups=True
            i += 2 if consumed_file else 1
            continue
        if a == '--':
            opt.inputs.extend(argv[i+1:]); break
        opt.inputs.append(a); i+=1
    if opt.file is not None and opt.inputs:
        eprint("error: the argument '--file <FILE>' cannot be used with '[INPUT]...'\n\nUsage: grex [OPTIONS] {INPUT...|--file <FILE>}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    if opt.surrogates and not opt.escape:
        eprint("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --escape\n\nUsage: grex [OPTIONS] {INPUT...|--file <FILE>}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    if opt.file is None and not opt.inputs:
        eprint("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  --file <FILE>\n  <INPUT>...\n\nUsage: grex [OPTIONS] {INPUT...|--file <FILE>}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    return opt

def split_lines_text(data: str) -> list[str]:
    if data == '': return []
    parts = data.split('\n')
    if parts and parts[-1] == '':
        parts = parts[:-1]
    return [p[:-1] if p.endswith('\r') else p for p in parts]

def read_inputs(opt: Options) -> list[str]:
    if opt.file is not None:
        fname = opt.file
        if fname == '-':
            fname = sys.stdin.read()
            # Rust's path handling tolerates a trailing line ending in this usage.
            fname = fname.rstrip('\r\n')
        try:
            with open(fname, 'rb') as f:
                data = f.read().decode('utf-8', 'surrogatepass')
        except Exception:
            eprint('error: the specified file could not be found\n')
            sys.exit(1)
        return split_lines_text(data)
    if len(opt.inputs)==1 and opt.inputs[0]=='-':
        data = sys.stdin.read()
        return split_lines_text(data)
    return opt.inputs

def filter_cases(cases: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    # Empty test cases are retained only if every provided test case is empty.
    if not cases:
        return []
    nonempty=[c for c in cases if c!='']
    if nonempty:
        cases=nonempty
    # de-duplicate after preserving deterministic sort-independent language.
    seen=[]; st=set()
    for c in cases:
        if c not in st:
            st.add(c); seen.append(c)
    return seen

def panic_no_cases():
    eprint("\nthread 'main' (0) panicked at /workspace/src/builder.rs:48:13:\nNo test cases have been provided for regular expression generation\nnote: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace\n")
    sys.exit(101)

def build_regex(cases: list[str], opt: Options) -> Expr:
    seqs=[]
    for c in cases:
        seq=preprocess_string(c,opt)
        if opt.repetitions:
            seq=compress_repetitions(seq,opt)
        seqs.append(seq)
    return generate_language(set(seqs), opt)

def main(argv):
    opt=parse_args(argv)
    cases=filter_cases(read_inputs(opt))
    if not cases:
        panic_no_cases()
    body=build_regex(cases,opt)
    start_anchor = not opt.no_start_anchor
    end_anchor = not opt.no_end_anchor
    if opt.verbose:
        out=render_verbose(body,opt,start_anchor,end_anchor)
    else:
        prefix='(?i)' if opt.ignore_case else ''
        out=prefix + ('^' if start_anchor else '') + body.render(opt, False) + ('$' if end_anchor else '') + '\n'
    if opt.colorize:
        out=colorize_regex(out)
    sys.stdout.write(out)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1:])

# ------------------------- low-level character handling ----------------------

def is_word_char(ch: str) -> bool:
    if ch in ('\u200c', '\u200d'):
        return True
    cat = unicodedata.category(ch)
    return ch.isalpha() or ch.isdecimal() or cat.startswith('M') or cat == 'Pc'

def lower_simple(s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        lo = ch.lower()
        if len(lo) == 1:
            out.append(lo)
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)

def unicode_escape(cp: int) -> str:
    return "\\u{" + format(cp, 'x') + "}"

def outside_escape(ch: str, escape_non_ascii: bool, surrogates: bool, verbose: bool=False):
    cp = ord(ch)
    if escape_non_ascii and cp > 0x7f:
        if surrogates and cp > 0xffff:
            u = cp - 0x10000
            hi = 0xd800 + (u >> 10)
            lo = 0xdc00 + (u & 0x3ff)
            # The original treats the surrogate-pair spelling as one atom, but
            # it must be grouped when quantified.
            return unicode_escape(hi) + unicode_escape(lo), False, False
        return unicode_escape(cp), False, True
    if ch == '\n': return "\\n", True, True
    if ch == '\r': return "\\r", True, True
    if ch == '\t': return "\\t", True, True
    if ch == '\v': return "\\v", True, True
    if ch == '\f': return "\\f", True, True
    if verbose and ch == ' ':
        return "\\ ", True, True
    if verbose and ch == '#':
        return "\\#", True, True
    if ch in r".\+*?()|[]{}^$-":
        return "\\" + ch, True, True
    return ch, True, True

def class_char_escape(ch: str, endpoint: bool=False) -> str:
    if ch == '\n': return "\\n"
    if ch == '\r': return "\\r"
    if ch == '\t': return "\\t"
    if ch == '\v': return "\\v"
    if ch == '\f': return "\\f"
    if ch in ('\\', '[', ']', '^', '-'):
        return "\\" + ch
    return ch

def build_char_class(chars: list[str]) -> str:
    vals = sorted(set(chars), key=lambda c: ord(c))
    parts = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(vals):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(vals) and ord(vals[j+1]) == ord(vals[j]) + 1:
            j += 1
        run_len = j - i + 1
        if run_len >= 3:
            parts.append(class_char_escape(vals[i], True) + '-' + class_char_escape(vals[j], True))
        else:
            for k in range(i, j+1):
                parts.append(class_char_escape(vals[k], False))
        i = j + 1
    return '[' + ''.join(parts) + ']'

# ------------------------------ AST classes ---------------------------------

class Expr:
    def render(self, opt: Options, verbose_token: bool=False) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError
    def max_len(self) -> int: return 0
    def min_len(self) -> int: return 0
    def min_string(self) -> str: return ''
    def contains_repeat(self) -> bool: return False
    def simple_inline(self) -> bool: return False

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Empty(Expr):
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False): return ''
    def simple_inline(self): return True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Atom(Expr):
    key: Any
    display: str
    verbose_display: str
    raw: str = ''
    charclassable: bool = False
    direct_quant: bool = True
    shorthand: bool = False
    orig_len: int = 1
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        return self.verbose_display if verbose_token else self.display
    def max_len(self): return self.orig_len
    def min_len(self): return self.orig_len
    def min_string(self): return self.raw if self.raw else self.display
    def simple_inline(self): return True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CharClass(Expr):
    chars: tuple
    text: str
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False): return self.text
    def max_len(self): return 1
    def min_len(self): return 1
    def min_string(self): return min(self.chars, key=lambda c: ord(c)) if self.chars else ''
    def simple_inline(self): return True

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Concat(Expr):
    parts: tuple
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        return ''.join(p.render(opt, verbose_token) for p in self.parts if not isinstance(p, Empty))
    def max_len(self): return sum(p.max_len() for p in self.parts)
    def min_len(self): return sum(p.min_len() for p in self.parts)
    def min_string(self): return ''.join(p.min_string() for p in self.parts)
    def contains_repeat(self): return any(p.contains_repeat() for p in self.parts)
    def simple_inline(self): return all(p.simple_inline() for p in self.parts)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Alt(Expr):
    alts: tuple
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        gp = '(' if opt.capture_groups else '(?:'
        return gp + '|'.join(a.render(opt, verbose_token) for a in self.alts) + ')'
    def max_len(self): return max((a.max_len() for a in self.alts), default=0)
    def min_len(self): return min((a.min_len() for a in self.alts), default=0)
    def min_string(self): return min((a.min_string() for a in self.alts), default='')
    def contains_repeat(self): return any(a.contains_repeat() for a in self.alts)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptionalExpr(Expr):
    child: Expr
    style: str = 'normal'  # 'normal' or 'prefix'
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        s = self.child.render(opt, verbose_token)
        gp = '(' if opt.capture_groups else '(?:'
        if self.style == 'prefix':
            # Prefixes generated before a common suffix are grouped a little more
            # aggressively by grex.
            if isinstance(self.child, Atom) and len(self.child.raw) == 1 and self.child.direct_quant and not self.child.shorthand:
                return s + '?'
            return gp + s + ')?'
        if isinstance(self.child, (Atom, CharClass)) and getattr(self.child, 'direct_quant', True):
            return s + '?'
        if isinstance(self.child, Alt):
            return s + '?'
        return gp + s + ')?'
    def max_len(self): return self.child.max_len()
    def min_len(self): return 0
    def min_string(self): return ''
    def contains_repeat(self): return self.child.contains_repeat()
    def simple_inline(self):
        return isinstance(self.child, (Atom, CharClass)) or (isinstance(self.child, Concat) and self.child.simple_inline() and self.style=='normal')

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RepeatExpr(Expr):
    base: Expr
    min_count: int
    max_count: int
    def render(self, opt, verbose_token=False):
        bs = self.base.render(opt, verbose_token)
        if self.min_count == self.max_count:
            q = '{%d}' % self.min_count
        else:
            q = '{%d,%d}' % (self.min_count, self.max_count)
        direct = isinstance(self.base, (Atom, CharClass)) and getattr(self.base, 'direct_quant', True)
        if direct:
            return bs + q
        gp = '(' if opt.capture_groups else '(?:'
        return gp + bs + ')' + q
    def max_len(self): return self.base.max_len() * self.max_count
    def min_len(self): return self.base.min_len() * self.min_count
    def min_string(self): return self.base.min_string() * self.min_count
    def contains_repeat(self): return True
    def simple_inline(self):
        return isinstance(self.base, (Atom, CharClass)) and getattr(self.base, 'direct_quant', True)

# Sequence item is an atom or a repetition atom. Both are hashable.
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RepeatItem:
    base_items: tuple
    base_expr: Expr
    count: int
    orig_len: int
    def to_expr(self):
        return RepeatExpr(self.base_expr, self.count, self.count)
    def max_len(self): return self.orig_len * self.count
    def min_len(self): return self.orig_len * self.count
    def min_string(self): return self.base_expr.min_string() * self.count

# -------------------------- preprocessing -----------------------------------

def shorthand_atom(name: str) -> Atom:
    return Atom(('sh', name), '\\' + name, '\\' + name, raw='\\'+name, charclassable=False, direct_quant=True, shorthand=True)

def make_literal_atom(ch: str, opt: Options) -> Atom:
    disp, cc, direct = outside_escape(ch, opt.escape, opt.surrogates, False)
    vdisp, _, _ = outside_escape(ch, opt.escape, opt.surrogates, True)
    # Non-ASCII escaped atoms are not put into character classes.
    charclassable = cc and not (opt.escape and ord(ch) > 0x7f)
    return Atom(('lit', ch, opt.escape, opt.surrogates), disp, vdisp, raw=ch, charclassable=charclassable, direct_quant=direct, shorthand=False)

def convert_char(ch: str, opt: Options):
    # documented precedence
    isdig = ch.isdecimal()
    issp = ch.isspace()
    isword = is_word_char(ch)
    if opt.digits and isdig:
        return shorthand_atom('d')
    if opt.spaces and issp:
        return shorthand_atom('s')
    if opt.words and isword:
        return shorthand_atom('w')
    if opt.non_digits and not isdig:
        return shorthand_atom('D')
    if opt.non_words and not isword:
        return shorthand_atom('W')
    if opt.non_spaces and not issp:
        return shorthand_atom('S')
    return make_literal_atom(ch, opt)

def preprocess_string(s: str, opt: Options):
    if opt.ignore_case:
        s = lower_simple(s)
    return tuple(convert_char(ch, opt) for ch in s)

# -------------------------- repetition detection ----------------------------

def item_key(x):
    if isinstance(x, Atom): return ('A', x.key)
    if isinstance(x, RepeatItem): return ('R', tuple(item_key(i) for i in x.base_items), x.count)
    return ('?', repr(x))

def items_equal_slice(seq, i, j, L):
    for k in range(L):
        if item_key(seq[i+k]) != item_key(seq[j+k]):
            return False
    return True

def expr_from_sequence_items(items: tuple, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    # Render a repeated unit using the ordinary generator, but without trying
    # suffix alternatives. This gives compact nested repetitions such as
    # (?:a{5}b){2} and (?:\d\s\w{3}\s){2}.
    if not items:
        return Empty()
    parts = []
    for it in items:
        if isinstance(it, Atom): parts.append(it)
        else: parts.append(it.to_expr())
    return concat_expr(parts)

def compress_repetitions(seq: tuple, opt: Options) -> tuple:
    n = len(seq)
    if n == 0: return seq
    candidates = []
    minL = max(1, opt.min_substring_length)
    threshold = opt.min_repetitions + 1
    for i in range(n):
        maxL = (n - i) // threshold
        for L in range(minL, maxL + 1):
            c = 1
            while i + (c+1)*L <= n and items_equal_slice(seq, i, i+c*L, L):
                c += 1
            if c >= threshold:
                # only keep the maximal count for this start/length
                candidates.append((L*c, L, i, c))
    # Prefer the longest covered region; tie: shorter repeated substring, earlier.
    candidates.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1], t[2]))
    occupied = [False]*n
    selected = []
    for span, L, i, c in candidates:
        if any(occupied[i:i+span]):
            continue
        for k in range(i, i+span): occupied[k] = True
        selected.append((i, L, c, span))
    selected.sort()
    by_start = {i:(L,c,span) for i,L,c,span in selected}
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        if i in by_start:
            L,c,span = by_start[i]
            unit_orig = tuple(seq[i:i+L])
            unit_compressed = compress_repetitions(unit_orig, opt)
            base_expr = expr_from_sequence_items(unit_compressed, opt)
            out.append(RepeatItem(unit_orig, base_expr, c, L))
            i += span
        else:
            out.append(seq[i])
            i += 1
    return tuple(out)

# ----------------------------- generation -----------------------------------

def concat_expr(parts: list[Expr]) -> Expr:
    flat = []
    for p in parts:
        if isinstance(p, Empty):
            continue
        if isinstance(p, Concat):
            flat.extend(p.parts)
        else:
            flat.append(p)
    if not flat: return Empty()
    if len(flat) == 1: return flat[0]
    return Concat(tuple(flat))

def alt_expr(alts: list[Expr], opt: Options, sort=True) -> Expr:
    # de-duplicate by compact rendering
    seen = set(); uniq = []
    for a in alts:
        k = a.render(opt, False)
        if k not in seen:
            seen.add(k); uniq.append(a)
    if sort:
        uniq.sort(key=lambda e: sort_key(e, opt))
    if not uniq: return Empty()
    if len(uniq) == 1: return uniq[0]
    return Alt(tuple(uniq))

def sort_key(e: Expr, opt: Options):
    # Default grex output generally lists longer branches first; when
    # repetition conversion is enabled, plain alternatives tend to precede
    # quantified ones and quantified alternatives are ordered by matched size.
    if opt.repetitions:
        rep = 1 if e.contains_repeat() else 0
        if rep:
            return (1, e.min_len(), e.min_string(), e.render(opt, False))
        return (0, -e.max_len(), e.min_len(), e.min_string(), e.render(opt, False))
    return (-e.max_len(), e.min_len(), e.min_string(), e.render(opt, False))

def atom_expr_from_item(it):
    if isinstance(it, Atom): return it
    if isinstance(it, RepeatItem): return it.to_expr()
    raise TypeError

def base_expr_for_items(items: tuple, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    return expr_from_sequence_items(items, opt)

def ranges_from_counts(counts: list[int]):
    counts = sorted(set(counts))
    ranges = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(counts):
        j = i
        while j+1 < len(counts) and counts[j+1] == counts[j]+1:
            j += 1
        ranges.append((counts[i], counts[j]))
        i = j+1
    return ranges

def atom_alternation(items: list, opt: Options, allow_mixed_class=True) -> Expr:
    # This handles a set of one-position alternatives, including character
    # classes and repeat-count ranges.
    # First, group RepeatItems with identical bases.
    used = [False]*len(items)
    exprs = []
    # Repeat groups
    repeat_groups: Dict[Any, list] = {}
    repeat_base: Dict[Any, tuple] = {}
    for idx,it in enumerate(items):
        if isinstance(it, RepeatItem):
            k = tuple(item_key(x) for x in it.base_items)
            repeat_groups.setdefault(k, []).append(it.count)
            repeat_base[k] = it.base_items
            used[idx]=True
    # Include a count of one for single-token literal bases only; this mirrors
    # the compact a{1,n} output while keeping ab|(?:ab){2,n} separate.
    for k, counts in list(repeat_groups.items()):
        base_items = repeat_base[k]
        if len(base_items)==1:
            for idx,it in enumerate(items):
                if not used[idx] and item_key(it)==item_key(base_items[0]):
                    counts.append(1); used[idx]=True
    for k, counts in repeat_groups.items():
        base = base_expr_for_items(repeat_base[k], opt)
        for a,b in ranges_from_counts(counts):
            if a==b==1:
                exprs.append(base)
            else:
                exprs.append(RepeatExpr(base,a,b))
    remaining = [it for idx,it in enumerate(items) if not used[idx]]
    # Char class grouping for literal atoms.
    literal_atoms = [it for it in remaining if isinstance(it, Atom) and it.charclassable]
    non_literals = [it for it in remaining if not (isinstance(it, Atom) and it.charclassable)]
    if literal_atoms:
        group_as_class = False
        if len(literal_atoms) >= 2 and not non_literals:
            group_as_class = True
        elif len(literal_atoms) >= 2 and allow_mixed_class:
            # Escaped unicode alternatives are mixed with classes; shorthand
            # conversions usually keep alphanumeric literals separate.  For
            # punctuation, a class is still what grex prints.
            has_shorthand = any(isinstance(x, Atom) and x.shorthand for x in non_literals)
            if not has_shorthand:
                group_as_class = True
            else:
                if all((not a.raw.isalnum()) for a in literal_atoms):
                    group_as_class = True
        if group_as_class:
            chars = tuple(a.raw for a in literal_atoms)
            exprs.append(CharClass(chars, build_char_class(list(chars))))
        else:
            exprs.extend(literal_atoms)
    exprs.extend(atom_expr_from_item(x) for x in non_literals)
    return alt_expr(exprs, opt, sort=True)

def seq_to_expr(seq: tuple, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    return concat_expr([atom_expr_from_item(x) for x in seq])

def language_key(seqs: Set[tuple]):
    return tuple(sorted(tuple(item_key(x) for x in s) for s in seqs))

def generate_prefix_normal(seqs_in, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    seqs = set(seqs_in)
    if not seqs:
        return Empty()
    if len(seqs)==1:
        return seq_to_expr(next(iter(seqs)), opt)
    has_empty = tuple() in seqs
    nonempty = {s for s in seqs if s}
    if not nonempty:
        return Empty()

    # If every sequence is a single item, render this level directly.
    if all(len(s)==1 for s in nonempty) and not has_empty:
        return atom_alternation([s[0] for s in nonempty], opt)

    # Build first-token groups, merging transitions with identical tail languages.
    tail_to_tokens: Dict[Any, list] = {}
    tailsets: Dict[Any, Set[tuple]] = {}
    for s in nonempty:
        first, tail = s[0], s[1:]
        k = language_key({tail})
        # Actually merge by the full set of tails for a token below; first collect
        # by first token then invert.
    token_to_tails: Dict[Any, Set[tuple]] = {}
    token_obj: Dict[Any, Any] = {}
    for s in nonempty:
        first, tail = s[0], s[1:]
        k = item_key(first)
        token_to_tails.setdefault(k,set()).add(tail)
        token_obj[k]=first
    inv: Dict[Any, list] = {}
    inv_tails: Dict[Any, Set[tuple]] = {}
    for k,tails in token_to_tails.items():
        lk = language_key(tails)
        inv.setdefault(lk,[]).append(token_obj[k])
        inv_tails[lk]=tails
    terms = []
    for lk,tokens in inv.items():
        token_expr = atom_alternation(tokens, opt)
        tail_expr = generate_language(inv_tails[lk], opt)
        terms.append(concat_expr([token_expr, tail_expr]))
    body = alt_expr(terms, opt, sort=True)
    if has_empty:
        return OptionalExpr(body, 'normal')
    return body

def generate_prefix_before_suffix(seqs_in, opt: Options) -> Expr:
    seqs = set(seqs_in)
    if tuple() not in seqs:
        return generate_prefix_normal(seqs, opt)
    nonempty = {s for s in seqs if s}
    if not nonempty:
        return Empty()
    # Build nonempty alternatives in normal fashion, but keep top branches.
    expr = generate_prefix_normal(nonempty, opt)
    if isinstance(expr, Alt):
        branches = list(expr.alts)
    else:
        branches = [expr]
